If no candidate passes the load pipeline, the outcome is `SL_LOAD_NO_LOADABLE_SAVE`: Save/Load publishes `SL_LOAD_NO_LOADABLE_SAVE` and `save_status`; the Chart Table shows it as a boot-flow screen — the kernel is not `RUNNING` and no pause is requested (CT-25) — with New campaign or Quit (the message text is UX's; how a running session whose death stub found nothing is torn down to the boot flow is OQ-42, and from that state the player must be able to reach New campaign or Quit, AC-SL-134) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; the dead world is never autosaved. The stub attaches no penalty beyond the lost interval. **The one plain line** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: on the first `RUNNING` frame the HUD shows one ship-log line naming the record that was restored (UI-11), through its `FIRST_FRAME_LINE` channel, keyed on `restore_reason = DEATH_STUB` and carrying the restored generation's playtime. Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): option (b) of OQ-46 (D15, D84). It is a HUD line, not a screen: it has no death wording, no sound and no dim-out, so the art bible's no-death-screen rule (7.4) stands. Failure Contract & Re-wake replaces this rule at VS-A through the same `request_restore` path and PROFILE store (SL-9). *(Superseded 2026-10-27 — design review, withdrawn in the re-review: the earlier ruling that the stub waits for the in-flight write before it bumps the epoch is gone. There is no wait at the `DEAD` boundary: a job that finished by the boundary is a candidate, a job still busy is abandoned (which bumps `write_epoch`), and `restore_epoch` is computed after, before selection, SL-23.)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
206	
207	**SL-8 — Generation selection and demotion.** *Default:* restore the **newest** generation that is not demoted and passes the pre-check (SL-11) — the user's rule, "restart from the last autosave", verbatim. Save/Load restores an *older* generation only when (a) the newest fails the pre-check (fall back newest-first, within `LOAD_MAX_ATTEMPTS`; a reproduction mismatch is never a fallback reason, SL-12), or (b) the **last restored** generation `g_r` (set by the death stub and by Continue alike) is the newest non-demoted verified generation (no newer one exists) **and** one of two routes fires, where `T_downed` is the start of the `DOWNED` episode that ended in `DEAD` (observed through the `loco_state` read SL-13 already grants) and a restore returns `T` to `T(g_r)`: the **RISKY-window route** — `g_r` is tagged `RISKY`, is not a `QUIT` generation unless its `risky_cause` contains `VITALS`, and `T_downed − T(g_r) ≤ DEATH_LOOP_WINDOW_TICKS` 3 600 — or the **fairness route** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* (Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): X7 (b), D14) — `T_downed − T(g_r) < W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE` (600 ticks at the defaults), **independent of `RISKY`**, and of the kind except that a `QUIT` generation without `VITALS` in its `risky_cause` is exempt *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling G2)* (OQ-52). The fairness route covers a capture taken one tick before `DOWNED` and a doom from hostile contact, a breach or lethal friendly fire that no tell announced: a generation that would wake the player into a fall they had under `W_MIN_WARNING_S` to perceive is skipped, which is the unfairness the Graph's `W_MIN_WARNING_S` exists to prevent. 208	
209	**SL-9 — PROFILE store (K OQ 13, D5).** A per-campaign `profile.sav` beside the generation files, in the same container (`file_kind = PROFILE`; no `state_hash`; the trailer and per-block hashes still apply). The kernel produces one snapshot; Save/Load **splits it by `persist_scope` at write time**: WORLD blocks to the generation, PROFILE blocks to `profile.sav`. An in-session restore (the death stub, a load of the already-open campaign) passes **only WORLD blocks** to `request_restore`, so PROFILE blocks are never rolled back (CR-18); a cold open (process start, Continue) loads each scope whole from its own file, because partial restore within a scope is unsupported. `profile.sav` is rewritten, by the same atomic procedure (SL-10), when a capture's PROFILE per-block hashes differ from those last written (no subscription needed), on QUIT, and on an owner change notification (mechanism provisional, as SL-13), which triggers a profile-only capture with no new generation; a floor `PROFILE_MIN_WRITE_GAP_TICKS` bounds the write rate. `profile.sav` keeps a permanent `.bak` (Pillar 5 makes it more precious than any one world generation). A new campaign starts with an empty profile; the death stub and the VS re-wake ("new crew, same world") leave PROFILE untouched, so knowledge survives death in memory by construction and the disk file matters across process restarts. **Zero PROFILE blocks ship in the MVP; the mechanism is specified and tested now** with a synthetic PROFILE block (the kernel's acceptance criterion for `PROFILE` blocks is the model). What is kept at re-wake is Failure Contract's policy. `scope` (SHARED / PER_PLAYER) and `persist_scope` (WORLD / PROFILE) are orthogonal axes: `suit.state` and the Sanity blocks `sanity.state` and `sanity.ledger` are `PER_PLAYER` × `WORLD` in the MVP and **roll back with the death stub**; only knowledge, lore and scars are PROFILE, and none ships. 211	**SL-10 — Write procedure and write epoch (D9; behaviour only → ADR candidate "atomic write, backup and thread model").** Capture is synchronous inside the kernel's `SAVING` state (the kernel owns capture cost against `SNAPSHOT_BUDGET_MS`, cited; Save/Load adds, on the main thread, only the encoding of the captured plain data and a small hand-off — Formula `write_budget`, bounded by `SAVE_ENCODE_BUDGET_MS` and `WRITE_HANDOFF_MAX_FRACTION`, both logging thresholds); the payload is an immutable byte value handed to a **worker** that never touches the kernel or any block [UNV: worker threads with file access]. The worker writes `gen_k.tmp` (named `gen_<write_epoch>_<k>.tmp`, SL-10 continued), flushes, re-reads and re-hashes it, renames the position's existing file (the oldest generation, if any) to `.bak`, renames `.tmp` into place, verifies again, deletes `.bak` and rewrites `campaign.json` (state table T-4 in States). **Rules:** every `store_*` return is checked (they return `bool` since Godot 4.4 — sourced from the engine reference); any false return, open error, hash mismatch or rename failure leaves every previous generation exactly as it was, reports to diagnostics and to `save_status`, and the next trigger retries with bounded exponential backoff (`AUTOSAVE_FAIL_BACKOFF_MAX_TICKS`; `AUTOSAVE_FAIL_ESCALATE_COUNT` consecutive failures raise the HUD notice). Never overwrite in place; never delete a generation before its successor verified; **never write while the kernel is `FAULTED`**. The design assumes only that a rename of a closed file to an *absent* name is all-or-nothing; atomic replace on Windows, sharing violations from scanners and indexers and OneDrive-redirected folders are [UNV] and are spike items. "Verified" means readable and hash-correct through the operating system's cache — it does not prove the bytes reached the media (whether a flush implies an fsync is [UNV]); the ring and the recovery scan (T-6) are the answer to power loss, not the verify step. **Write epoch (`write_epoch`)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R1)*: this in-memory, per-process counter was called the "session epoch" and is renamed so it cannot be confused with the persisted `restore_epoch` of SL-23; wherever this GDD says "the epoch" in a write context (`gen_<write_epoch>_<k>.tmp`, `STALE_EPOCH`, "epoch bump", "epoch++"), it means `write_epoch`. Every `request_restore` increments `write_epoch`, which each write job carries; a job that observes an advanced `write_epoch` before its first rename aborts and removes its `.tmp`; a job that had already completed its swap lands a verified generation of the abandoned timeline, which is moved to `quarantine/` as `STALE_EPOCH` and is never a candidate (otherwise a later death would restore the ghost of the previous timeline). Recovery on opening a campaign runs the crash-point scan of T-5: any `*.sav`, `*.bak` or `*.tmp` that verifies is accepted and ordered by `generation`; a file that cannot be proven obsolete is never deleted.

213	**SL-10 (continued) — writer thread contract, polling and abandonment** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. *Hand-off.* The worker receives only the per-block `PackedByteArray`s (immutable, caller-owned, *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*), file paths and integers (position, generation, `write_epoch`, retry counts): no kernel reference, no block, no Node and no `Callable` that touches the scene tree, and it never calls `call_deferred` into Save/Load or waits on the main thread. It publishes a status record (`state` ∈ the T-4 write states, `write_epoch`, `generation`, `position`, result code) under a `Mutex` [UNV: the status publication pattern is confirmed by the spike]; the main thread only **polls** that record and never joins the worker, because `Thread.wait_to_finish` and `WorkerThreadPool.wait_for_task_completion` take no timeout, so a join at the `DEAD` boundary would hang the frame on a hung write and could deadlock a worker that reports back through `call_deferred` [UNV: confirmed by the spike, AC-SL-90]. *Polling.* A tick-boundary poll in `RUNNING`; a frame poll from the Save/Load Node with `process_mode = PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS` [UNV: confirmed in `PAUSED` and `LOADING`] in `PAUSED`, `LOADING`, `SAVING` and during the quit wait, where no tick runs and a tick-boundary poll would never fire. *`DOWNED` entry.* When a bound seat enters `DOWNED` with a job in flight, the main thread sets the job's `finish_or_abort` flag in the status record: the worker completes only its required steps, takes no rename retries beyond the first, skips the manifest rewrite (a hint) and aborts at its first failure, removing its `.tmp`; `DEATH_STUB_WRITE_WAIT_MS` stays the shorter limit that starts at `DOWNED` entry. *Abandon semantics.* To abandon a job the main thread increments `write_epoch`, logs `SL_WRITE_ABANDONED_AT_DEATH` (or `SL_WRITE_ABANDONED_TIMEOUT` when a deadline expired), takes the job out of `writer_busy` (an abandoned job never counts toward the hard gate, so one hung worker cannot disable every later autosave) and records its ring position as **claimed**: F-9 skips claimed positions until the job reports, and if no unclaimed position other than the newest generation's remains, the write ends `FAILED` with `SL_WRITE_NO_POSITION` and backs off. The worker re-reads `write_epoch` from its status record immediately before each ring-touching rename and aborts (removing its `.tmp`) if it is stale; a job that lands a generation despite that (the check-then-rename race, or a worker that resumed after being stuck past the check) reports its old `write_epoch`, and the main thread moves the file to `quarantine/` as `STALE_EPOCH`, never a candidate (SL-3). The worker is never killed. *Owner.* Capture and every `request_*` call stay on the main thread; the single Save/Load Node (SL-6, close mechanism) owns the worker handle and the poll. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **Thread model, reaping, exit, lock.** *Model:* one `Thread` per job (no `WorkerThreadPool`), its handle held on a `RefCounted` `WriteJob` object that also carries the status record, so the thread's lifetime is the job's. *Reaping:* each poll (tick-boundary or frame) calls `wait_to_finish()` on a job whose thread reports `!is_alive()`; a job that is not alive and has published no terminal `WRITTEN` or `FAILED` status is a worker killed by a GDScript error: `SL_WRITE_WORKER_DIED`, `save_status` reads `FAILED`, `fail_n` is incremented, the ring position is released and the `.tmp` is left to T-6, instead of the 30 s `WRITE_JOB_TIMEOUT_MS` hold of the hard gate. *Cap:* at most `MAX_LIVE_ABANDONED_JOBS` (default 2) abandoned workers may be alive at once; at the cap a new write ends `FAILED` with `SL_WRITE_TOO_MANY_ABANDONED` and backs off until one reports. *Exit:* process exit never blocks on a busy or abandoned worker (no `wait_to_finish` on a live thread); a `QUIT` write that is itself busy follows SL-6's timeout, and an abandoned worker still running at exit is left to the OS, its `.tmp` handled by T-6 on the next open. *Single instance:* the campaign directory is opened under an exclusive lock (`campaign.lock`, created with an exclusive open and holding the process id; the mechanism and its behaviour under OneDrive and antivirus are [UNV], spike rows in AC-SL-30 and AC-SL-90); a second process that cannot take it opens the campaign **READ_ONLY**: it writes no generation, runs no T-6 deletion or quarantine move and offers New campaign and Quit only (AC-SL-147), because two processes would collide on `gen_` and `.tmp` names and T-6 would delete the other process's work.

274	**SL-17 — Zero blocks, zero hooks (D13).** Save/Load registers no state block and no step hook: ring bookkeeping lives in `campaign.json`, because a WORLD block would roll back on restore and desync the file set from the world. The failed-write notice and the main-menu newest-record line are inviolable channels (H5): their look is UX's, but they never take flesh or violet, never flicker with sanity and are never a hallucination class; there is no per-write glyph *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*. Because Suit vitals and the Sanity level roll back with the world, a reload is also never a sanity cure (H3).

323	| 6 | Pre-check order and names | Trailer SHA before the layout id, JSON and version judgement (SL-1 format law: the layout-id byte is inside the SHA-covered range); one closed `SL_PRECHECK_*` set (22 pre-kernel steps, plus the post-restore compare) | lead-programmer; reorders R10 |

329	### States and Transitions
330	
331	Save/Load owns no kernel state and no state block (SL-17). It has **host-local** state — `last_save_T`, `pending_event` (kind only; events coalesce), `first_due_T`, `restore_epoch`, the writer's state, `restored_gen_id` (the generation this session began from) and per-generation `suspect` counters in `campaign.json` — all re-derived on process start (`last_save_T := T` of the restored generation, `pending_event := none`, `first_due_T := none`), none of it sim state, none of it able to alter the sim **except `restore_epoch`**, which is persisted in the generation headers (SL-23) and is the one Save/Load value the sim sees, through `kernel.clock` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R1)* (an autosave-transparency criterion in Acceptance Criteria). 332	
333	**T-1. Kernel-state interplay, from Save/Load's seat.**
334	
335	| Kernel state | What Save/Load may do | What it must not do | Rule |
336	|---|---|---|---|
337	| `BOOTING` | Run the block-contract boot assertions on the frozen registry | Issue any request; read a file as a world | SL-15 |
338	| `LOADING` | Wait; publish `restore_reason`; hold the epoch; verification window (dev/test; release diagnostic-only per SL-12, K-4 provisional) | Issue a second request (the kernel ignores and reports it); autosave | SL-11, SL-12 |
339	| `RUNNING` | Poll the gate and triggers; `request_snapshot` when an autosave fires; `request_restore` on crew death | `request_pause` / `request_resume` (not its calls) | SL-4, SL-7 |
340	| `PAUSED` | Save & Quit `request_snapshot`; `request_restore`: dev-build `load(generation)` only (no MVP caller) | Start an interval autosave (`T` cannot advance, so none is due) | SL-6, SL-11 |
341	| `SAVING` | Wait. A restore requested now waits for the boundary | Queue a second snapshot | SL-10 |
342	| `FAULTED` | Show recovery; on explicit user action `request_restore` of the newest verified generation; `request_shutdown` | **Any write**, any autosave, any overwrite | SL-22 |
343	| `SHUTTING_DOWN` | Nothing — the QUIT write completed (`WRITTEN`) before the request was issued | Begin any write | SL-6 |
344	
345	**T-2. Autosave scheduler (host-local).**
346	
347	| State | Entry | Exit | Transitions | Who may cause them |
348	|---|---|---|---|---|
349	| `IDLE` | Boot; a write ended; a restore reset `last_save_T` | `due` becomes true (interval elapsed, or an event is pending and `AUTOSAVE_MIN_GAP_TICKS` has elapsed) or a QUIT is requested | → `DUE_WAITING`; → `FIRING` (QUIT; soft conditions bypassed; refused with `SL_QUIT_NO_WRITE_DOWNED` while any seat is `DOWNED`/`DEAD`) | Clock `T`; event notifications (provisional); the pause panel |

351	| `FIRING` | `request_snapshot` issued at a boundary | Capture handed to the writer (T-4 `CAPTURING`) | → `IDLE` on `WRITTEN`; → `BACKOFF` on `FAILED` | Kernel (`SAVING`); the writer |
352	| `BACKOFF` | A write failed | The backoff interval elapses (bounded exponential, capped by `AUTOSAVE_FAIL_BACKOFF_MAX_TICKS`) | → `DUE_WAITING` (the save is still due, because `last_save_T` is unchanged by a failed write) | Clock |

460	**What Save/Load exposes and consumes, in names fixed elsewhere.** It registers **no hooks, no mutators, no commands (the VS-B `saveload.request_save` is reserved and provisional), no blocks and no dirty keys** (SL-17), and it never writes a block (H3, H4). It calls the kernel's host-local control plane — `request_snapshot`, `request_restore`, `request_shutdown` (CR-15); `request_pause` / `request_resume` are the pause panel's, not its own. It reads `kernel.clock`, `controller.state.loco_state` per bound seat, the Graph's `failures()` read view and an optional Attention SIM view (SL-13). It publishes the host-local reads `save_status`, `SaveInfo` and `restore_reason` and the API of SL-21. All three rules for every consumer in the kernel's Interactions section hold: a system that wants state to persist registers a block and never talks to Save/Load directly. **Every interface with an undesigned or in-flight system below is provisional — it lists only what that system must supply or may rely on, never a guess of its internals.**

518	## Formulas
519	
520	All sim-time quantities are **integer ticks** read from `kernel.clock.T` and converted to seconds only in examples, at `TICK_RATE` 60 (registry, cited). Anything hashed or stored in a header is an integer or an exact-width hex string (S-1); a millisecond budget below is a float used only for logging thresholds, is never hashed or replicated, and so is outside the kernel's determinism rule. **Cited, never restated:** `state_hash` (kernel D.12, registry), `rng_derive` (kernel D.10, registry), `snapshot_bytes` and `capture_time_ms` (kernel D.11), `SNAPSHOT_BUDGET_MS` and `MAX_BLOCKS` (kernel GDD values, not registry entries — kernel registry candidates), `DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS` (registry, Controller), `W_MIN_WARNING_S` (registry, Graph). Owned constants are named in Tuning Knobs. Ten formulas follow; the first six are the registry candidates of the rulings (R29, with `generation_select` and `save_verification` amended at the stage-5 checkpoint), the last four are derived bounds and encodings the criteria need.
521	
522	### F-1. `autosave_due`
523	
524	The `autosave_due` formula is defined as:
525	
526	`elapsed = T − last_save_T; interval_due = elapsed ≥ AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_TICKS; event_due = (pending_events ≠ ∅) AND elapsed ≥ AUTOSAVE_MIN_GAP_TICKS AND NOT (ragged_breach_open() AND ASSEMBLY_CUT ∈ kinds(pending_events)); due = interval_due OR event_due; kind = EVENT if event_due else AUTO` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
527	
528	**Variables:**
529	
530	| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
531	|---|---|---|---|---|
532	| `T` | int | 0 … 2^63 − 1 | `kernel.clock` (read at the tick boundary) | Current sim tick |
533	| `last_save_T` | int | 0 … `T` | Save/Load session memory: the capture `T` of the newest durable generation; reset to the restored generation's `T` on every restore | Basis of the loss window; unchanged by a failed write, so a failed save stays due |
534	| `event_pending` | bool | {0, 1} | Owner notifications and pure reads (SL-4): `POD_ARRIVED` (`web_events`), `last_shape_change_T()` (Assembly), Interaction's `last_salvage_T()` (BS-21) — `POD_ARRIVED` provisional until merge; coalesced; cleared when a capture at or after the event's tick is `WRITTEN` | At least one autosave-worthy event (pod-hop arrival, weld or cut completion, dock, section extraction) since the last write. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* `event_pending` is the predicate `pending_events ≠ ∅`, where `pending_events` is a **set of `(kind, tick)` entries**, not one coalesced kind: a later event adds an entry and never overwrites an earlier one, and an entry leaves the set only when a capture at or after its tick is `WRITTEN` |
535	| `event_kind`, `ragged_breach_open()` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | enum, bool | {`ASSEMBLY_WELD`, `ASSEMBLY_CUT`, …}; {0, 1} | Assembly pure reads (`last_shape_change_T()` names the kind, MSA-33; `ragged_breach_open()` is true while a RAGGED cut still has an uncapped stub; registered, source Modular Ship Assembly) | The ruled withhold (D54): a RAGGED cut's `ASSEMBLY_CUT` is not due while the breach is open; `event_pending` stays latched and the event is taken once it is capped. `ASSEMBLY_WELD` and a SEALED cut (no stubs, so the read is false) are never withheld by their own entry. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* While a RAGGED cut's entry is pending and the breach is open, **no entry of any kind** fires a capture, so a cut followed by a weld cannot capture inside the open breach (the weld entry waits with the cut); event order no longer matters |
536	| `AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_TICKS` ★ | int | 5 400 … 18 000, default 10 800 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | Tuning Knobs | Interval trigger (3 min) |
537	| `AUTOSAVE_MIN_GAP_TICKS` ★ | int | 900 … 3 600, default 1 800 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | Tuning Knobs | Floor between any two `AUTO`/`EVENT` generations; strictly below the interval |
538	| `elapsed` | int | 0 … unbounded | calculated | Sim ticks since the last durable capture |
539	| `due`, `kind` | bool, enum | {0, 1}; {`AUTO`, `EVENT`} | calculated | Input to F-2; `kind` is stored in the header and `SaveInfo` (an event and the interval due on the same tick produce **one** save, kind `EVENT`) |
540	
541	**Output Range:** boolean `due` plus `kind`. `T < last_save_T` cannot occur after the reset-on-restore rule; if observed, `elapsed := 0`, `last_save_T := T` and `SL_AUTOSAVE_CLOCK_REGRESSION` is logged once. No interval save is ever due while the kernel is `PAUSED` (`T` cannot advance). The `QUIT` kind is a separate path (SL-6, F-2) and never passes through `due`.
542	
543	**Example:** `last_save_T = 432 000` (the anchor moment, Player Fantasy). A weld completes at `T = 437 400`: `elapsed = 5 400 ≥ 1 800`, so `event_due`, `due = 1`, `kind = EVENT`. The next interval save is then due at `437 400 + 10 800 = 448 200`. Latch case: a second event at `T = 438 700` has `elapsed = 1 300 < 1 800`, so `event_pending` stays set and `due` becomes true at `T = 439 200`. **Withhold case** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: a RAGGED cut applies at `T = 440 000` with `last_save_T = 437 400` (the anchor weld's save) and two uncapped stubs: `elapsed = 2 600 ≥ 1 800` but `ragged_breach_open()` is true, so `event_due = 0` and `event_pending` stays latched; the last stub is capped at `T = 441 800` (`elapsed = 4 400`), `event_due = 1`, and the capture fires on the next retry-grid tick. If the interval falls due at 448 200 with the breach still open, `assembly_breach_block` defers it (F-2) and it fires no later than 455 400, tagged `RISKY` with `risky_cause = {ASSEMBLY_BREACH}`; a SEALED cut at the same `T` has no stubs and is due at once. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* **Cut then weld:** with the RAGGED cut of `T = 440 000` pending and two stubs open, a weld completes at `T = 440 900`; `pending_events = {(ASSEMBLY_CUT, 440 000), (ASSEMBLY_WELD, 440 900)}`, `ragged_breach_open()` is true, so `event_due = 0` at every grid tick until the last stub is capped at `T = 441 800`, then one capture fires and clears both entries (AC-SL-146).
544	
545	### F-2. `autosave_gate`
546	
547	The `autosave_gate` formula is defined as:
548	
549	`refractory_block = (last_recover_T ≠ none) AND (T − last_recover_T) < W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE; hard_block = (EXISTS seat IN bound_seats: loco_state(seat) IN {DOWNED, DEAD}) OR kernel_state NOT IN {RUNNING, PAUSED} OR writer_busy OR restore_pending OR refractory_block; graph_tell_block = EXISTS d IN graph.failures(): d.subject_kind IN {NODE, EDGE, SEAM} AND d.cause == ENDOGENOUS AND d.sev ≥ 1 AND d.warn_elapsed < W_MIN_STEPS; attention_tell_block = tell_active AND (gate_tell_mode == STRICT OR tell_remaining < W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE); tell_block = graph_tell_block OR attention_tell_block; vitals_block = EXISTS seat IN bound_seats: vitals_state(seat) ≥ CRITICAL; assembly_breach_block = ragged_breach_open(); soft_block = tell_block OR breach_phase ≠ CALM OR (EXISTS seat: loco_state(seat) IN GATE_SOFT_STATES) OR vitals_block OR assembly_breach_block; waited = T − due_first_T; next_retry_T = (fail_n == 0 ? 0 : last_fail_T + min(AUTOSAVE_RETRY_TICKS × 2^min(fail_n − 1, 16), AUTOSAVE_FAIL_BACKOFF_MAX_TICKS)); fire = due AND waited mod AUTOSAVE_RETRY_TICKS == 0 AND T ≥ next_retry_T AND NOT hard_block AND (NOT soft_block OR waited ≥ AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS); risky = fire AND soft_block; risky_cause = the members of {GRAPH_TELL, ATTENTION_TELL, BREACH_PHASE, SEAT_STATE, VITALS, ASSEMBLY_BREACH} whose input is true at the fire tick (empty iff NOT risky); quit_write = kernel_state IN {RUNNING, PAUSED} AND NOT (EXISTS seat: loco_state(seat) IN {DOWNED, DEAD}); quit_risky = quit_write AND soft_block` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
550	
551	**Variables:**
552

752	## Edge Cases
753	
754	Each case names the exact outcome and, where one exists, the diagnostic id. Diagnostics (`SL_*`) are log and `save_status` entries; they are not a second refusal set — the closed refusal set is `SL_PRECHECK_*` (T-5) and the boot set is `SL_BOOT_*` (SL-15). Cases are grouped by theme; a rule id in parentheses names where the behaviour is defined. **Reading rule for every case:** the kernel is never touched by a file the pre-check refuses, and the previous generations are never changed by a failed write.
755	
756	### Zero, maximum and out-of-range values
757	
758	- **If `world_seed` is 2^63 or above, or `T` exceeds 2^53**: the header stores each as exactly 16 lowercase hex characters and the round trip is bit-exact (F-10); a signed GDScript read of a `world_seed` above 2^63 − 1 is negative [UNV] and must still round-trip. Any other width, an uppercase letter or a non-hex character is refused (`SL_PRECHECK_HEADER_HEX_MALFORMED`, CORRUPT). Rationale: S-1 — a float parse loses everything above 2^53.
759	- **If a header number that must stay a number (`generation`, a length, an offset) arrives at or above 2^53 or with a fraction**: the float parse has already rounded it, so the pre-check refuses (`SL_PRECHECK_HEADER_FIELD_NOT_INT`, CORRUPT). Rationale: a silently rounded `generation` would corrupt ring order.
760	- **If `header_len` is 0, a corrupt 4 GiB, or larger than the file allows**: refused at the `header_len` bounds step before any allocation (`SL_PRECHECK_HEADER_LEN_INVALID`, CORRUPT). Only a re-signed file can reach this step, because the trailer step comes first; the fuzz includes re-signed files for exactly that reason.
761	- **If the encoded file would exceed `MAX_SAVE_BYTES`, a block exceeds `MAX_BLOCK_BYTES`, or the header exceeds `MAX_HEADER_BYTES` at write time**: no file is produced (`SL_WRITE_TOO_LARGE{block}`), `save_status` reads `FAILED`, the ring is untouched and play continues; nothing is truncated. Rationale: the write side never produces a file its own read side would refuse (F-6).
762	- **If the size crosses `SAVE_SIZE_ALARM_BYTES`**: the write proceeds and `SL_SIZE_ALARM` is logged once per campaign open. Rationale: it is a prompt to review compression at VS-A, not a failure.
763	- **If the header `codec` is not 0**: refused at the `format_version` step (`SL_PRECHECK_FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED`, INCOMPATIBLE). Rationale: the field is reserved with no decode path in the MVP, which also rules out decompression bombs.
764	- **If `T < last_save_T` is observed**: `elapsed := 0`, `last_save_T := T`, and `SL_AUTOSAVE_CLOCK_REGRESSION` is logged once. Rationale: unreachable after the reset-on-restore rule, so it is a defect signal; dev builds assert.
765	- **If `kernel.clock.T` cannot be read as an integer**: `SL_BAD_CLOCK`, no write and no restore. Rationale: every interval and window is in ticks (SL-23); with no clock, no decision is safe.
766	
767	### Simultaneous rules and same-tick collisions
768	
769	- **If a Graph warning window opens on the tick the interval falls due, or a second window opens as the first closes** *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*: the save waits (`graph_tell_block`, F-2), re-evaluated on the retry grid; chained windows are bounded by `AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS`, after which the save fires tagged `RISKY`. Rationale: the Graph's `W_MIN_WARNING_S` guarantee must not be shortened by a restore, and the cap keeps `loss_ticks` unchanged.
770	- **If the only open Graph window belongs to a dormant section**: its `warn_since_step` is frozen (Graph dormant-section rule) so it cannot close; until the Graph owner answers OQ-38 the save can wait to the cap and be tagged `RISKY`. Rationale: a rare, bounded exposure that is recorded rather than hidden.
771	- **If an event and the interval fall due on the same tick**: one save, kind `EVENT` (F-1). Rationale: the ring must not be flushed by two generations a frame apart.
772	- **If a due autosave falls inside the post-`DOWNED` refractory** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: it waits (`refractory_block`, F-2) and fires on the first retry-grid tick at or after `last_recover_T + W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE`; the cap does not shorten it, and a `QUIT` is not bound by it (SL-6). Rationale: a recovery reopens the gate onto a seat that may still be in the state that downed it (user ruling X7 (c)).
773	- **If a seat's `vitals_state` is `CRITICAL` when the save falls due and stays so past the cap** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: the save defers to `AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS` and is then written `RISKY` with `risky_cause` containing `VITALS`; nothing is drawn. Rationale: SL-5 row (c) is capped like every soft input, so a suit that never recovers cannot suppress saving forever.
774	- **If an `ASSEMBLY_CUT` event is latched while `ragged_breach_open()` is true** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: the event is not due and stays latched, the interval save is deferred as a soft input meanwhile, and the event is taken once the breach is capped (F-1, F-2; user ruling D54). Rationale: a restore from a save inside a self-inflicted decompression can reload the player into an unwinnable breach that the autosave hides; the interval path is bounded by the cap, by which time the decompression has resolved either way.
775	- **If a due autosave and the `DEAD` tick share a boundary**: no snapshot is taken; `DEAD` is a hard condition and the restore wins (SL-7). Rationale: a snapshot of a dead world is the trap the gate exists to prevent.
776	- **If no `DOWNED` episode was observed before `DEAD`**: `T_downed := T_dead` for `generation_select`, and the hard condition still closes the gate at that boundary. Rationale: the formula must not depend on an observation Save/Load may not have made.
777	- **If `request_restore` arrives while the kernel is `SAVING`**: the kernel waits for the boundary (K:651) and the capture completes; the death stub then settles the writer (SL-7): the new generation is a candidate only if its write has reached `WRITTEN` by that boundary, otherwise its job is abandoned. The combination should not occur at all, because `DOWNED` precedes `DEAD` by 1 800 ticks on the timer (at least `GIVE_UP_MIN_TICKS` after a `give_up`) and the hard gate refuses captures while a seat is down; seeing it is a defect signal. Rationale: no main-thread wait on a write job, so a hung worker cannot hold the death stub *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
778	- **If a Save & Quit and an interval autosave are due at the same tick**: the `QUIT` path wins and the pending autosave state is discarded (`due_first_T` is session memory only); only an in-flight write delays it. Rationale: the quit writes the current state anyway.
779	- **If Continue is pressed while the kernel is `LOADING`**: the second call is ignored (`SL_LOAD_REENTRANT`), as the kernel also ignores and reports a second request. Rationale: one restore at a time, one `restore_epoch` step.
780	- **If the death stub fires before the initial `NEW_GAME` generation is `WRITTEN`**: the stub finds the baseline job `WRITTEN` (then it is the candidate) or settles it as in SL-7: a job still busy is abandoned, there is no candidate, and the escalation of SL-18 applies (`SL_NEW_GAME_NO_BASELINE`, the empty directory removed, the menu); a `FAILED` baseline takes the same path *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. Rationale: the 30 s `DOWNED` floor (0.8 s after a solo `give_up`, user ruling D7) makes the case nearly unreachable, but a campaign with no verified generation must never reach a first death.
781	
782	### Writing, crashing and recovering (save/restore)
783	
784	- **If the process is killed during `WRITING_TMP`**: the position's file is intact and a partial `gen_k.tmp` remains; the next open deletes the `.tmp` and the ring is unchanged (T-6). Rationale: an unverified `.tmp` is never a candidate.
785	- **If the process is killed between `SWAPPING_OUT` and `SWAPPING_IN`**: `gen_k.bak` and a complete `.tmp` exist with no `gen_k.sav`; recovery promotes the `.tmp` if it verifies and deletes the `.bak`, otherwise promotes the `.bak` back (T-6). Rationale: at least two verified generations exist during any swap because `AUTOSAVE_GENERATIONS` is at least 2.
786	- **If a `store_*` call returns false, a file will not open, or disk is full or locked**: the `.tmp` is removed best-effort, previous generations are untouched, `save_status` reads `FAILED` (`SL_WRITE_FAILED{step}`), `last_save_T` is unchanged so the save stays due, and the retry backs off to at most `AUTOSAVE_FAIL_BACKOFF_MAX_TICKS`; after `AUTOSAVE_FAIL_ESCALATE_COUNT` consecutive failures the HUD notice is raised. Rationale: sourced — `FileAccess.store_*` returns `bool` since 4.4 (breaking-changes), so every return is checked.
787	- **If a rename fails with a sharing violation (antivirus, indexer)**: the worker retries `RENAME_RETRY_COUNT` times, `RENAME_RETRY_DELAY_MS` apart, then rolls back by renaming the `.bak` back and reports `FAILED`. Rationale: the design assumes only that renaming a closed file to an absent name is all-or-nothing [UNV].
788	- **If a write job outlives a restore**: a job that sees an advanced `write_epoch` before its first rename aborts and removes its `.tmp` (`SL_WRITE_ABORTED_RESTORE`); a job already past `SWAPPING_IN` lands a verified generation of the abandoned timeline, which is moved to `quarantine/` as `STALE_EPOCH` and is never a candidate. An **abandoned** job (SL-10) leaves `writer_busy` at once, its `.tmp` carries the old `write_epoch` in its name and its ring position stays claimed until it reports; a later autosave goes ahead on another position *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Rationale: otherwise a later death would restore the ghost of the previous timeline.
789	- **If two files carry the same `generation` (a kill between renames)**: prefer `.sav` over `.bak`, then verified over unverified; the loser is removed only after the winner verifies. Rationale: order is the header number, so the choice is deterministic.
790	- **If `campaign.json` is missing, corrupt or disagrees with the files**: it is rebuilt by scanning headers (`SL_MANIFEST_REBUILT`) and a load is never refused for it; demoted and quarantined generations stay excluded because they are encoded in file names, while `suspect` counters and REBASED baselines are lost. Rationale: the manifest is a hint, never truth (SL-3).
791	- **If `AUTOSAVE_GENERATIONS` shrinks between builds (3 → 2)**: the writer only uses positions `0 … N − 1`; a file at a position beyond `N` stays on disk as a candidate by generation order and is removed only by the campaign delete. If it grows, new positions fill lazily as the first free position. Rationale: never delete a file that cannot be proven obsolete.
792	- **If a restore moves `T` backwards**: `last_save_T := T(g)`, `due_first_T` and `event_pending` are cleared and `restored_gen_id := g`; generation numbers keep rising and the first new autosave is `AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_TICKS` after `T(g)`. Rationale: timers are sim time and the sim just went back.
793	
794	### Hostile, damaged and foreign files (pre-check)
795	
796	- **If a file is empty, shorter than the size floor, or truncated anywhere**: `SL_PRECHECK_FILE_TOO_SMALL` or `SL_PRECHECK_FILE_SHA_MISMATCH` (CORRUPT); the file is a quarantine candidate and the loader falls back. Rationale: a missing or short trailer is truncation, detected for free.
797	- **If one bit flips in the last byte of the magic (the layout-id byte)**: the trailer no longer matches, so the file is CORRUPT (`SL_PRECHECK_FILE_SHA_MISMATCH`), not INCOMPATIBLE, and the loader falls back on an intact ring. Rationale: the layout id is judged only after the trailer (SL-1 format law); a flipped bit must not stop the loader.
798	- **If one bit flips in `format_version`**: the same — corruption, falling back — never "made by a newer build". Rationale: the integrity steps precede the compatibility steps.
799	- **If the newest generation is genuinely newer (a re-signed `format_version` above ours, or `min_reader_version` above ours)**: INCOMPATIBLE — the loader stops with "made by an incompatible build", files stay in place, and the campaign directory is `READ_ONLY` for the older build; New campaign creates a different directory. Rationale: a silent fallback would roll the player back and then overwrite newer files (SL-11).
800	- **If an older generation is loadable but the newest is INCOMPATIBLE**: no fallback occurs and no older generation is overwritten. Rationale: same-campaign files share the incompatibility in practice, and a rollback is data loss.
801	- **If a block id is unknown and not on `RETIRED_BLOCKS`**: INCOMPATIBLE, the loader stops (`SL_PRECHECK_UNKNOWN_BLOCK`), so the kernel's `RESTORE_UNKNOWN_BLOCK` is unreachable — reaching it would be a Save/Load defect. If it is on `RETIRED_BLOCKS`, it is stripped with `SL_PRECHECK_RETIRED_BLOCK_STRIPPED` and the mode becomes REBASED (cause 2). Rationale: a removed block must not strand old saves; an unknown one is a newer or foreign build.
802	- **If a non-mandatory block is missing and its `added_in_format` exceeds the file's `format_version`**: `default_state()` fills it with a note and the mode becomes REBASED (cause 3); otherwise `SL_PRECHECK_MANDATORY_MISSING` (CORRUPT). Rationale: K:645 leaves the decision to Save/Load.
803	- **If a `PERCEPTION_OUT` block, or a block of the wrong `persist_scope`, appears in a file**: `SL_PRECHECK_PERCEPTION_BLOCK_PRESENT` or `SL_PRECHECK_SCOPE_MISMATCH` (CORRUPT). Rationale: Save/Load never writes one, so presence is a defect or tampering, and a PROFILE block inside a world file could roll knowledge back.
804	- **If a payload contains an `Object` marker, a forbidden type, excessive nesting or too many nodes**: `SL_PRECHECK_BLOCK_TYPE_FORBIDDEN` or `_BLOCK_DECODE_LIMITS` (CORRUPT); no object is instantiated and the kernel is never touched. Rationale: the object-disallowed decode stops instantiation but does not itself bound allocation (SL-2).
805	- **If a Graph payload stores a packed array as a JSON-style number list (an S-1 violation that survives the container)**: it passes the container checks, because the pre-check validates declared types, and the Graph's two-phase `restore()` refuses it (`GRAPH_RESTORE_BAD_TAG`) with the live Graph block byte-identical; the kernel enters `FAULTED` (blocks restored earlier in `restore_after` order are not rolled back, K:650), the menu offers Continue on the remaining candidates (SL-22), and the generation's failure counter increments. Rationale: owner-level validation cannot run before the kernel is touched; the 1,000-mutation fuzz (re-signed files) measures how rare this path is.
806	- **If header `T` or `world_seed` differs from the `kernel.clock` block although every hash is valid (a re-signed file)**: `SL_PRECHECK_HEADER_CLOCK_MISMATCH` (CORRUPT). Rationale: the header copy exists for exactly this cross-check.
807	- **If a file's `campaign_id` differs from its directory name (a file copied between campaigns, or a directory renamed)**: `SL_PRECHECK_CAMPAIGN_MISMATCH` (CORRUPT), quarantine candidate. Rationale: a copied directory under the same name from another machine is untrusted data under the same caps and loads if it passes; a renamed one does not.
808	- **If the header `hash_algo` is not implemented by this build**: the file stage still runs (SHA-256 is Save/Load's own), the compare is skipped (`SL_VERIFY_ALGO_SKIPPED`) and the mode is REBASED (cause 4); it is never a refusal. Rationale: a kernel hash change must not break saves (SL-16).
809	- **If stale `.tmp` or `.bak` files exist when a campaign opens**: the recovery scan of T-6 reconciles them before the first load; nothing it cannot prove obsolete is deleted. Rationale: a crash can leave any of them.
810	- **If `seats` names a PlayerId the session has not bound**: allowed; the session rebuilds its binding table (CR-7) and the owners' restores decide. A `PER_PLAYER` key outside `seats`, or an empty or duplicated `seats`, is `SL_PRECHECK_SEATS_INVALID`. Rationale: identity is the seat, never the transport peer.
811	
812	### Death stub and generation selection (degenerate strategies live here too)
813	
814	- **If a write job is still busy at the `DEAD` boundary (a hung worker)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: it is abandoned (`SL_WRITE_ABANDONED_AT_DEATH`), `write_epoch` advances, the stub selects among the already-verified candidates, and a later autosave runs on a fresh job with epoch-named temporary files; if the stuck worker ever resumes, its late rename is quarantined as `STALE_EPOCH` (AC-SL-130). Rationale: a join on a hung write would hang the frame, and a blocking wait with no timeout is not available on the engine's thread API.
815	- **If the only candidate is `RISKY` and a loop is detected**: it is restored anyway and `SL_STEPBACK_NONE_AVAILABLE` is logged. Rationale: the user rule is restart from the last autosave; there is nothing older.
816	- **If a `RISKY` generation is restored, the crew dies inside the window, and the predecessor is chosen**: the `RISKY` file is renamed `gen_k.demoted`; a second death before any new autosave restores the predecessor again, never the demoted one (the three-death scripted fixture). Rationale: without demotion the ring would oscillate between a `RISKY` newest and its predecessor.
817	- **If the newest generation is not `RISKY` and the crew dies repeatedly at the same spot** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: the newest is restored every time (the user rule) unless a fall comes within `W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE` ticks of the restore, when the fairness route steps back whether or not the generation is `RISKY`; `deaths_per_restored_gen` is counted in diagnostics for playtest. Rationale: the general step-back from a non-`RISKY` generation is the question left to playtest (OQ-1); only the fairness window was ruled (X7 (b)).
818	- **If every candidate fails the pre-check**: `SL_LOAD_NO_LOADABLE_SAVE` is published before the kernel is touched; the Chart Table shows it as a boot-flow screen (no pause is requested, CT-25; in-session teardown, OQ-42) with New campaign or Quit; no file is deleted and the dead world is never autosaved. Rationale: the game stays inside the player's control and the files stay available for recovery.
819	- **If only demoted generations remain loadable**: a second pass restores the newest demoted one. Rationale: a stepped-back-from file is still better than nothing.
820	- **If the stub fires on a campaign with no restore yet (the first life)**: no loop is possible (`g_r` is none) and the newest generation, the `NEW_GAME` baseline at worst, is restored. Rationale: the formula needs a restored generation to detect a loop.
821	- **If the crew goes `DOWNED` within `W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE` (600) ticks of a restore, or later** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: within 599 ticks of `T(g_r)` the fairness route steps back (F-3: the generation is demoted, the predecessor is restored, `SL_STEPBACK_NONE_AVAILABLE` if there is none); from 600 ticks on, even inside `AUTOSAVE_MIN_GAP_TICKS`, the same non-`RISKY` generation is restored again and the loop rule does not apply. Rationale: under ten seconds of acting time is the unfair case; beyond it only a `RISKY` generation is suspected of being unwinnable.
822	- **If deaths follow a restore by under 600 ticks again and again** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: each death steps one generation further back (the generation stepped back to becomes `g_r` and the test repeats), bounded by the ring and ending at `SL_STEPBACK_NONE_AVAILABLE` on the last candidate. Rationale: every step costs the player a death and more lost time, so it is a price and not a prize; see the deliberate-fast-death case under degenerate strategies.
823	- **If the player ends the `DOWNED` wait with the solo `give_up` action** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* (user ruling D7): `DEAD` follows at the apply tick, at least `GIVE_UP_MIN_TICKS` after `T_downed`; the stub, `T_downed` and the selection are identical to the timer path, and a write job still busy is abandoned (SL-7). The loss floor is `GIVE_UP_MIN_TICKS + 1` (F-7) and metric M2 counts the death, with `death_via_give_up` logged as a separate column. Rationale: the Controller owns the action; Save/Load sees only `DEAD`.
824	- **If a seat reaches `DEAD` in the pod** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* (statuses run in the pod, user ruling D60): the path is identical: the hard gate was closed while the seat was `DOWNED`, the stub restores the newest verified generation, and `web.state` restores the leg and the pod. `IN_POD` is a soft state (SL-5), so a generation written earlier in the leg restores the in-leg state. Rationale: Save/Load keys on `loco_state` only.
825	- **If `DEAD` is entered during a camera cut**: the request is made at that tick's boundary, the Presenter holds the down sheet's last frame, and no second cut is issued (the Controller's edge case). Rationale: only `DEAD` during a *cut channel* is impossible, because `DOWNED` precedes it by 1,800 ticks on the timer (at least `GIVE_UP_MIN_TICKS` after a solo `give_up`, user ruling D7) and clears the channel *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
826	- **If an owner's `restore()` or `post_restore()` fails inside `LOADING`**: the kernel enters `FAULTED` with the prior state not intact; the loader does not retry in line; the menu's Continue re-runs the pipeline on the remaining candidates (SL-22). Rationale: K:170 allows only an explicit user restore out of `FAULTED`.
827	- **If a reproduction mismatch is detected (EXACT mode)**: release marks the generation `suspect` and plays on; dev and test halt; the loader never walks to another generation. Rationale: the bytes are proven, the defect is in the code, and it would reproduce on every generation.
828	- **If the compare window is missed (`kernel.clock.T` ≠ header `T`)**: `SL_VERIFY_WINDOW_MISSED`, no verdict, play on. Rationale: a hash taken after a tick has run would differ for the wrong reason (SL-12).
829	
830	### Save & Quit and window close
831

831	### Save & Quit and window close
832	
833	- **If a Save & Quit is requested while any bound seat is `DOWNED`**: nothing is written — `save_and_quit` returns `SL_QUIT_NO_WRITE_DOWNED`, `save_status` is unchanged, and shutdown proceeds after the hold-to-confirm "quit without saving"; Continue then restores the newest verified generation. Rationale: no file on disk may ever hold a `DOWNED` or `DEAD` seat; the death stub would have restored the same file within `DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS`.
834	- **If a Save & Quit is requested while a seat is `DEAD`**: unreachable in the solo MVP (the stub fires on the `DEAD` tick); the clause exists for multi-seat futures. Rationale: SL-6.
835	- **If a Save & Quit is requested with only a soft condition closed (a tell, a breach phase, `CHANNELLING`, `STAGGERED`, `IN_POD`, a `CRITICAL` suit, an open self-inflicted breach)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: the generation is written immediately and tagged `RISKY` with its `risky_cause`; inside the post-`DOWNED` refractory with a healthy suit it is written and is not `RISKY`. Rationale: refusing to quit traps the player; quitting without writing silently discards up to one interval.
836	- **If a Save & Quit finds the state hash equal to the newest generation's (same `T`, nothing changed)**: the write is skipped (`SL_QUIT_DEDUPED`) and shutdown proceeds. Rationale: a duplicate generation would only push a useful one out of the ring.
837	- **If the Save & Quit write fails or times out (`SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS`)**: the quit is held, `save_status` reads `FAILED`, the pause panel stays, and the player may retry or quit without saving by hold-to-confirm. Rationale: never silently lose progress; never trap the player.
838	- **If the window is closed while a write is in progress** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the quit waits up to `SAVE_QUIT_TIMEOUT_MS` (frame-polled, SL-6), then **holds**: `save_status` reads `FAILED`, `quit_held` is published and the player leaves only through the hold-to-confirm "quit without saving"; the next open reconciles by the crash table (T-6). Rationale: one outcome for a failed or slow quit, the one SL-6 and AC-SL-45c already state; an exit after a timeout would silently discard up to one interval.
839	- **If the window is closed while the kernel is `PAUSED` under the open Chart Table (SOLO)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass)*: Save/Load's handler runs `save_and_quit()` from `PAUSED` (`PAUSED → SAVING → PAUSED`) under SL-6's rules, then `request_shutdown`; the Chart Table calls nothing (EC-CT-38). **On a boot-flow screen** nothing is written and the process ends through boot code (ASK-CT-11). Rationale: one save path, the same rules everywhere.
840	- **If a quit is requested while the kernel is `FAULTED`**: no write is attempted (K:151); the quit proceeds to the menu or shutdown. Rationale: the faulting session is never saved over an existing generation.
841	- **If the window is closed while a seat is `DOWNED`, while the kernel is `LOADING`, or while it is `SAVING`** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: `DOWNED` writes nothing and holds the close for the hold-to-confirm "quit without saving" (`SL_QUIT_NO_WRITE_DOWNED`); `LOADING` defers the close intent until the kernel is `RUNNING` and then handles it as a `RUNNING` close; `SAVING` lets the in-flight job reach `WRITTEN` or `FAILED` and then dedupes against it or writes the `QUIT` generation (SL-6, close mechanism; AC-SL-44b). Rationale: every state has one answer and none of them is a silent exit.
842	- **If a Save & Quit is made while a Graph warning window is open** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the generation is written at once and tagged `RISKY`; Continue restores a fault with less than `W_MIN_WARNING_S` of its warning left. It is not clamped (a clamp would trap the player at the menu to protect a window they can see) and it is counted by metric M4. Rationale: SL-6.
843	
844	### PROFILE store
845	
846	- **If `profile.sav` is absent and zero PROFILE blocks are registered (every MVP build)**: this is valid on a cold open — an empty profile. Rationale: nothing to restore, nothing to refuse.
847	- **If `profile.sav` is absent and one or more PROFILE blocks are registered**: `SL_PRECHECK_MANDATORY_MISSING` for the profile file (CORRUPT class); `profile.sav.bak` is tried first, and if it is also unusable the world still loads, the profile is reset to `default_state()` with `SL_PROFILE_RESET`, and the damaged file is quarantined, never deleted. Rationale: Pillar 5 says knowledge is not lost with the ship, and a corrupt knowledge file must not strand the world.
848	- **If a PROFILE write is pending when a world restore occurs**: the profile is flushed first (its file is not part of the restore) and the restore then proceeds; a world restore never reads `profile.sav` into WORLD blocks. Rationale: CR-18 — partial restore within a scope is unsupported, and PROFILE blocks are never rolled back by a world restore.
849	- **If the process is killed during a PROFILE write**: the crash table (T-6) applies to `profile.sav` and its permanent `.bak`; the ring is unaffected. Rationale: a profile is rewritten by the same atomic procedure.
850	
851	### Hallucination interplay (Pillars 1 and 4)
852	
853	- **If a save is captured while a hallucination is active**: the file holds the true SIM state — the sanity level and the owner's counters — and never the perception output (`PERCEPTION_OUT`) or a field describing what the player saw. Rationale: a save is ground truth (H1); the rebuilt output after load derives from level and seed.
854	- **If the crew reloads after dying to a scrubber that "looked fixed" because of a false system state** *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*: Save/Load restores every persisted counter and seed exactly (kernel G4, D.10), reads no perception and varies nothing by it; whether the false state's onset replays at the same moment or is re-keyed is Sanity & Hallucination Rules' decision (OQ-37). The physical fact underneath, that the scrubber fails at minute four, is unchanged and is Pillar 1. Rationale: binding perception replay here would let the player memorise hallucinations across deaths (P2, P4); any re-keying must not be steerable by quit or death. Threat draws (the ambush replayed at the same corner) are re-keyed per restore epoch by user ruling D16 (OQ-47, SL-23): the physical fact replays, the ambush does not *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
855	- **If the sanity level was low at death**: the restore returns the generation's sanity level (WORLD-scoped) — death does not cure sanity (H3), so no "die to clear your head" exploit exists. Rationale: Suit vitals and the Sanity level roll back with the world.
856	- **If the first `RUNNING` frame after `LOADING` is presented unfiltered**: this violates H4; the requirement is routed to the Perception Filter, Sanity and Pipeline (OQ-11), and the black hold covers any rebuild. Rationale: one clean frame would be a free oracle.
857	- **If an autosave would vary its timing, or a save list its contents, with sanity**: not allowed and not built; Save/Load never reads perception (SL-24). Rationale: a lie that reached the save menu would be unfalsifiable inside the session.
858	
859	### Co-op hooks and later tiers
860	
861	- **If a guest later joins (VS-B)**: the snapshot payload is separable from the file wrapper (SL-1) and is the guest's initial transfer (CR-18); a guest's save request is the reserved `saveload.request_save` command (provisional — Co-op Session & Replication), validated on the host; no guest-authoritative block exists. Rationale: host-owned saves only.
862	- **If one of several seats is `DEAD` while others live (multi-seat futures)**: the hard condition keeps autosave closed until Failure Contract & Re-wake resolves the seat (provisional — Failure Contract undesigned), so the deferral is unbounded in that case. Rationale: recorded as a gap for VS-A/VS-B, not designed here.
863	- **If a friendly-fire death occurs (VS-B)**: the save records the `DEAD` seat's state like any death and never records blame (Anti-pillar: no PvP). Rationale: blame is Failure Contract's.
864	- **If a peer reconnects under a different transport id**: nothing in any save changes — blocks are keyed by PlayerId (SL-20). Rationale: "keyed by peer id" is a stale token.
865	- **If `TICK_RATE` differs between the build that wrote a file and the build reading it**: INCOMPATIBLE at the `tick_rate` step (`SL_PRECHECK_TICK_RATE_MISMATCH`); the kernel's `TICK_RATE_MISMATCH` is the unreachable backstop. Rationale: a save is bound to the rate that wrote it.
866	
867	### Versioning and migration
868	
869	- **If a golden v1 save is loaded by a build whose Graph migrates v1 to v2**: the mode is REBASED (cause 1), the load succeeds, the recomputed hash becomes the baseline in `campaign.json`, and the next autosave writes the new shape; the old file is not rewritten. Rationale: a downgrade followed by an upgrade must not half-migrate a file (SL-14).
870	- **If a save from a development build predates the first build given to anyone outside the project**: it may be refused with "made by an incompatible development build" — migration is an obligation only from that build on (SL-14). Rationale: the policy is Save/Load's own; the Layout open question that the Graph cites is unverified (OQ-12).
871	- **If a new persisted block is registered while dev saves exist** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: every older dev save now lacks a mandatory block and carries a different `registry_epoch`, so each is INCOMPATIBLE-dev ("made by an incompatible development build"), not CORRUPT, and none is quarantined (T-5 step 21). Rationale: otherwise each new block would quarantine every dev save as damaged and hide it from the owner.
872	- **If a new persisted block is added after the first outside build**: `format_version` increments, `min_reader_version` equals the new version, the container migration is the identity and the new block is filled by `default_state()` (SL-14). Rationale: the friction of adding a block stays constant.
873	
874	### Degenerate strategies and accepted exposures
875	
876	- **If the player kills the process (task manager, power loss) after a mistake** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: Alt-F4 and the title-bar close are not kills; they raise the window-close request and take the Save & Quit path, SL-6)*: the game falls back to the newest generation, a rewind of at most `AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_TICKS + AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS` = 18 000 ticks (mean about 5 400 ticks, 10 800 at most when no soft input defers the save, 18 600 on the narrow recovery-at-the-cap path, F-7; the user accepted this fault loss window, D55) — the same price as dying, minus the death floor (49 ticks with the give-up, 1,801 on the timer) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. Accepted and unpreventable (no write can protect against a kill); measured by M3 below (OQ-25). Rationale: both rewinds cost at most the minutes since the last autosave and nothing else.
877	- **If the player Save & Quits before a risky door, relaunches and Continues** *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*: it works as a retry of the player's inputs, and because the physical world is deterministic it can also reveal what is behind the door for up to the minutes since the last autosave. Accepted for the MVP as a bounded exposure (the user's death rule is binding; the Zomboid comparison does not carry over, because a Zomboid death is final), **but with a measurable trigger, not an open-ended "if playtest shows"**: metric M3 below. The interval is not the remedy, because a `QUIT` generation is written at the quit: the response is to keep the metric and escalate to Failure Contract & Re-wake, never deleting the `QUIT` generation (OQ-25) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Rationale: SL-6.
878	- **If the player dies on purpose to rewind a bad decision or to scout a room** *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*: the cost is at least `GIVE_UP_MIN_TICKS + 1` = 49 ticks with the solo `give_up` (1,801 on the timer) plus the time back to the last autosave, the restore also returns vitals and sanity, and in a deterministic world the physical death can reveal one visible unknown (Discovery, aesthetic priority 1) for about 3 to 5.7 minutes of sim time; threat draws re-key per restore epoch (D16), so a scouted ambush does not replay *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. Accepted for the MVP; metric M2 below is the trigger *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. Rationale: Pillar 5's design test — safe farming versus scarcity — resolves to scarcity, as long as scouting deaths stay rare.
879	- **If the player dies deliberately fast to step the ring back** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: a fall within `W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE` ticks of a restore demotes the restored generation and restores its predecessor (the fairness route, SL-8), so a player can choose to rewind further. Accepted: each step costs a death and strictly more lost time, depth is bounded by `AUTOSAVE_GENERATIONS`, and it buys only the older state, never a better one than a normal death could reach; metrics M1 and M2 see it (`deaths_per_restored_gen` and `scout_death_rate`). Rationale: the fairness route is the ruled price of never waking into an unfair fall (X7 (b)).
880	- **If the player treats event saves as checkpoints (event-scum)** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: a weld, cut, module cut, pod arrival or berth writes a generation (`EVENT_TRIGGERS`), so a player can learn that finishing a weld "saves" and plan a risky sortie around it, the bonfire pattern this document rejects. Accepted for the MVP with metric M5 as the trigger; the response is a data change (remove the offending trigger from `EVENT_TRIGGERS`) before touching the interval. Rationale: OQ-44, confirmed by the user (D17) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
881	- **If a save file is edited by hand and re-signed**: it loads if it passes the pre-check; integrity guards accidental damage, not tampering (host-owned, no PvP, no leaderboard). Rationale: documented scope of SL-16; a stricter trust model is a security-audit question before multiplayer.
882	
883	**Playtest triggers for the accepted exposures** *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*. Pillar 5's "loss costs ship and body" and Discovery (aesthetic priority 1) pull in opposite directions here, so the exposure is accepted with numbers attached. The constants below are playtest-protocol values, not data-file knobs, and are provisional starting values to be calibrated at the first outside build (AC-SL-94). `T_enter` is, at the MVP, the derelict-level first boarding `FIRST_BOARDED{derelict_id, T}` published by Web Map & Transit (WM-28; the dock room), not a compartment-level first entry, which no designed system tracks; a DIAGNOSTIC-only compartment-entry log (Debug Overlay, from Body section changes; never persisted) is the recorded refinement if M2 proves too coarse (OQ-25) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass)*. Wall-clock gaps come from `created_unix` file metadata and the process-start log, read by the playtest harness only, never by the sim (H9).
884	
885	| Metric | Definition | Starting threshold | Named response |
886	|---|---|---|---|
887	| **M1** `deaths_per_restored_gen` | Deaths whose restored generation is the same `generation`, counted per tester | Median across testers ≥ 3, or any tester ≥ 5 | Players are stuck on the same save, so death is too dear: lower `AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_TICKS` by up to 3 600 ticks (not below 5 400, OQ-19); if M1 trips again, ask the user OQ-1 (non-`RISKY` step-back) |
888	| **M2** `scout_death_rate` | Deaths with `T_dead − T_enter` ≤ `SCOUT_DEATH_WINDOW_TICKS` 5 400 (provisional protocol value: the 1 800-tick `DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS` timer floor plus 3 600 ticks of looking; with the solo `give_up` the real floor is `GIVE_UP_MIN_TICKS`, so the window admits up to 5 352 ticks of looking, and the log records `death_via_give_up` as a separate column) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*, divided by all deaths; evaluated for a tester with ≥ 4 deaths | More than 0.25 of that tester's deaths, in at least 2 of 3 testers | Death is being used as a free look: raise `AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_TICKS` by up to 3 600 ticks (not above 18 000) and raise `LOSS_CEILING_TICKS` by the same amount on purpose, because the defaults sit exactly on the ceiling and I9 refuses a release build above it; if M2 trips again in the next round, escalate to Failure Contract & Re-wake at VS-A |
889	| **M3** `quit_relaunch_rate` | Save & Quit followed by Continue within `QUIT_RELAUNCH_WINDOW_S` 120 s of wall time, divided by all `QUIT` generations | More than 0.30 of `QUIT` generations, or 3 or more such pairs inside one 30-minute session | *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Quit-and-relaunch is a disguised manual save. Raising the interval has **no effect** on a `QUIT` generation, so it is not the response: accept the exposure for the MVP, keep the metric, and on a repeat trip escalate to Failure Contract & Re-wake at VS-A *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R1: because every restore advances `restore_epoch`, a quit-and-relaunch also re-keys the next threat draws, so M3 now also measures use of that reroll; USER DECISION at OQ-50)*; never delete the `QUIT` generation (SL-8) and never add save-anywhere (OQ-18 allows only the pinned main-menu slot, and only for M1) |
890	| **M4** `quit_in_tell_rate` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | `QUIT` generations written with a Graph or Attention tell open, divided by all `QUIT` generations; read from the playtest build's write log (the gate inputs at each write, a DIAGNOSTIC log, never persisted) | More than 0.10 | The player quits inside a warning window and Continue restores a shortened warning (SL-6): ask the Graph owner for the loaded-descriptor query (OQ-38) and, if it persists, route to Failure Contract & Re-wake; never clamp the quit |
891	| **M6** `risky_generation_rate` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | `RISKY` generations divided by all generations, with per-cause counts over `risky_cause` (`GRAPH_TELL`, `ATTENTION_TELL`, `BREACH_PHASE`, `SEAT_STATE`, `VITALS`, `ASSEMBLY_BREACH`) from the write log; the sheet also logs E[loss \| death] (the mean loss over the deaths that actually happened), not the unconditioned mean of F-7 | More than 0.25 of all generations, or any single cause above 0.10 | The gate has seven soft inputs, and if `VITALS` or `ASSEMBLY_BREACH` is common the effective checkpoint spacing quietly became `I + D` and step-backs fire often: lower `AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS` once (not below 1 800, I2, I3), ask the Suit owner for the `CRITICAL` threshold (SE-33) or Assembly for the breach-window length; on a repeat trip escalate to Failure Contract & Re-wake at VS-A |
892	| **M5** `event_scum_rate` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | Event-kind generations followed by a death, or by a Save & Quit and Continue, within `SCOUT_DEATH_WINDOW_TICKS` of the event, divided by all event-kind generations; evaluated for a tester with ≥ 4 events | More than 0.30 for at least 2 of 3 testers | Players are using events as checkpoints: remove the offending trigger from `EVENT_TRIGGERS` (a data change, OQ-44) before touching the interval |

1056	## Game Feel
1057	
1058	The player never feels a save system; they feel what it guarantees (Player Fantasy: trust without a safety net). The feel of this system is therefore a set of **absences and one half-second**, each with an owner and a measurable target. Save/Load owns the timing of the two moments below; it owns no animation, sound or camera move.
1059	
1060	**1. A save is imperceptible.** *Feel:* the world runs continuously and the ship "just exists". *Target:* the main-thread cost Save/Load adds to the kernel's capture (`t_file_encode + t_handoff`, F-5) keeps the main-thread sum `main_hitch_ms` inside one frame at 60 Hz (`SNAPSHOT_BUDGET_MS` 16.7, cited); the file write, flush, re-read and rename run off the critical path (SL-10); no frame within ±2 frames of a capture start has CPU frame work above the baseline P99 plus `SAVE_HITCH_BUDGET_MS` (AC-SL-91; an absolute 16.7 ms cap cannot hold when the frame already spends 8 to 12 ms), and the CPU-work trace around a write is within `SAVE_HITCH_BUDGET_MS` / 2 between a gate-open run and a gate-deferring run (AC-SL-131) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. *What would feel wrong:* a stutter every three minutes that teaches the player when the game saved — it would turn every autosave into a small event and hand the player a rhythm to exploit — and, for the same reason, any per-write mark: there is none, because a mark shown on every write and held by the gate would make its absence a signal that danger is building (P2, P3) *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*. *Owner:* the kernel owns capture cost; Save/Load owns the added encode and hand-off; no system owns a glyph, because none exists.
1061	
1062	**2. A death is a breath of black, then recognition.** *Feel:* "death is a bitch. It happens." The loss lands in the body of the game, not in an interface: the avatar goes `DOWNED` for up to 30 seconds (`DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS` 1 800, the Controller's grief window and the real tension; the solo player may end it sooner with `give_up`, user ruling D7 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*), then on the `DEAD` tick the stub restores. The player sees layer-1 black for **at least 120 ms** (the `TRANSIT_HOLD` fade; shorter reads as a flash or a glitch) and **at most about 2 s** (longer reads as a crash); `LOADING_TARGET_MS` 1 000 (provisional) is the budget inside that corridor, measured as `restart_ms` (F-8). The first `RUNNING` frame is a hard camera `CUT` at the **pre-load zoom** (`k_z` is kept), so the player's framing is unchanged and recognition is instant: *I am back at the weld. The ship is exactly as I made it. I know what is in that room now.* *What would feel wrong:* a death screen, a sting, a "you died" line (the plain record line of UI-11 is the one permitted line: it states a time, not a death, user ruling D15), a lights-out beat (2.10 is for the cryo re-wake, VS-A), a zoom reset, a menu asking which save to load, or any penalty beyond the lost minutes — each would turn consequence into ceremony or punishment. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* A restore must also not release a burst of catch-up ticks on its first frame: the tick driver's wall-time accumulator is discarded on entry to `RUNNING` (K-5, routed to the kernel owner, OQ-45; AC-SL-132).
1063	
1064	**3. The cost of dying is a number the designer can feel.** The player pays the minutes since the last autosave and nothing else: at the defaults the mean is about 7 200 ticks (2 minutes), each death discards at most 20 400 ticks (5.7 minutes) on a healthy writer and 24 000 after one step-back (for a death whose `DOWNED` episode is the first since the last capture; each revive-and-fall-again adds up to 1 799, F-7) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, and a step-back chain can cost 39 000 (10.8 minutes) of reached progress (F-7) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. `AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_TICKS` is the main lever of how much death hurts, together with the event set (OQ-19, OQ-44): too cheap and "safe farming" returns, which Pillar 5 rejects ("scarcity that pushes inward"); too dear and death becomes a quit. These are playtest-owned numbers, measured by the 3-person kill/continue playtest (AC-SL-94) against the triggers M1 to M6 in Edge Cases, not design of consequence.
1065	
1066	**4. The refusal, not the rescue.** The autosave gate (SL-5) is felt only as an absence: the game never records a moment it could have warned the player about, because a world in a `DOWNED` state, in the ten seconds after a recovery, with a critical suit or with a Graph warning window still open, is never recorded *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. The player does **not** feel rescued — the save never buys back a mistake (no save-anywhere, SL-4) and the physical world's draws are restored exactly, so the room that killed them kills them again if they walk the same path (SL-23); threat draws re-key per restore (D16), so the ambush does not *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. Hallucination interplay *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)*: a reload is never a cure (H3) and Save/Load adds no window onto truth; whether a false state replays at the same moment is Sanity's decision, with the constraint that death and quit offer no reroll oracle (H2, OQ-37).
1067	
1068	**5. Failure is quiet and honest.** A failed write shows the plain `FAILED` notice only after `AUTOSAVE_FAIL_ESCALATE_COUNT` (3) consecutive failures; a corrupt newest generation is a one-line ship-log message and a fall back to the one before it; an incompatible build refuses to touch the campaign. None of these ever frightens: the system's tone is the opposite of the world's.
1069	
1070	**Who owns the feel.** Black-hold timing, fade and camera `CUT`: Pixel-Perfect Render Pipeline & Camera (cited). The `DOWNED` grief window (30 s, or the player's own `give_up`): Player Controller & Input. The UI-11 record line: HUD & Suit Layer *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. The failure notice: HUD & Suit Layer (designed — hud-and-suit-layer.md); the main-menu newest-record line: Chart Table (designed). The re-wake beat that will replace the bare stub: Failure Contract & Re-wake (VS-A, provisional — undesigned). The filter on the first frame: Perception Filter (designed; OQ-11). Save/Load owns the numbers in this section that are its own: `LOADING_TARGET_MS`, `AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_TICKS`, and `AUTOSAVE_MAX_DEFER_TICKS` (the written-hold of the status read is retired). Evidence: AC-SL-84, AC-SL-91, AC-SL-93, AC-SL-131 and AC-SL-132 (retained screenshots and frame-time logs, lead sign-off).

1161	
1162	1. **AC-SL-01 (auto) — S-1 fixture, bit-exact.** GIVEN a fixture with `world_seed = 2^64 − 1`, `T = 2^53 + 1`, and a Graph-shaped stand-in block holding `PackedInt64Array` and `PackedByteArray` fields, WHEN a generation is written and read back, THEN the header carries `world_seed` as `"ffffffffffffffff"` and `T` as `"0100000000002000"` (16 lowercase hex characters, little-endian, F-10) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*, the restored `kernel.clock` and every packed field are bit-identical, and the header contains no JSON number above 2^53. Cites: SL-1, SL-2, F-10.
1163	2. **AC-SL-02 (auto) — hex is exact-width.** GIVEN headers whose `T` is `"FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF"`, `"ffffffffffffffff0"`, `"ffffffffffffff"` or `"gggggggggggggggg"`, WHEN the pre-check runs, THEN each is refused `SL_PRECHECK_HEADER_HEX_MALFORMED` and the kernel spy records zero calls. Cites: F-10, T-5.
1164	3. **AC-SL-03 (auto) — numbers stay numbers below 2^53.** GIVEN a re-signed header whose `generation` is `9007199254740993` or `1.5`, WHEN the pre-check runs, THEN it is refused `SL_PRECHECK_HEADER_FIELD_NOT_INT`. Cites: SL-1, S-1.
1165	4. **AC-SL-04 (auto) — layout and trailer law.** GIVEN a generation file, WHEN its last 32 bytes are compared with SHA-256 over `[0, size − 32)`, THEN they are equal for every file the writer produces, for layout-id value 1 and for a synthetic future layout-id value. Cites: SL-1 (format invariant).
1166	5. **AC-SL-05 (auto) — objects are never decoded.** GIVEN a payload containing an `Object` marker, a `Callable`, a `Resource` path or nesting beyond `MAX_DECODE_DEPTH`, WHEN the pre-check decodes it, THEN it is refused (`SL_PRECHECK_BLOCK_TYPE_FORBIDDEN` or `_BLOCK_DECODE_LIMITS`), zero objects are instantiated, and the kernel spy records zero calls. Cites: SL-2, T-5.
1167	6. **AC-SL-06 (lint) — no object-allowing decode or Resource path** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. GIVEN the Save/Load source, WHEN searched for the symbols `bytes_to_var_with_objects`, `var_to_bytes_with_objects`, `ResourceLoader`, `ResourceSaver`, `load(`, `preload(` on a user path, `.tres`, `.res` and `instance_from_id`, THEN there are zero hits outside the lint fixture; the lint is proven by a positive control (a fixture file containing each symbol makes it fail) and a negative control (the shipped source passes). **Gate: BLOCKING** (it guards the object-injection boundary; promoted from "recommended").
