("145. **AC-SL-145 (auto, integration) — the three required restore-epoch cases and their failure paths** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R1)*. (i) GIVEN one save restored twice (stub then stub, or Continue then Continue, in one process), THEN the epochs are `e + 1` and `e + 2` and the kernel-derived threat draws (a spy on the kernel's `counter_eff` derivation, same `rng_counter`) differ. (ii) GIVEN the process killed after `EPOCH_DURABLE` and a fresh process that Continues the same slot, with `campaign.json` deleted before the relaunch, THEN the epoch advances again (`e + 2`), read from the headers; GIVEN the newest file deleted while a `.bak` or a `quarantine/` header carries a higher value, THEN the new value exceeds it. (iii) GIVEN the same (save bytes, `restore_epoch`) pair run twice to `T + 3 600`, THEN `state_hash` and every draw are identical. (iv) GIVEN the header-only rewrite failing (injected), THEN `SL_RESTORE_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` is logged, play proceeds, and the next generation's header carries the value; GIVEN a kill at each step of the rewrite (the fault-injection harness, T-6), THEN recovery finds a verifying file holding the old or the new value and never neither, and two files with one `generation` are ordered by `restore_epoch`. (v) GIVEN `restore_epoch = 2^32 − 1`, THEN the next restore saturates and logs, and no header is written with a value ≥ 2^32. (vi) GIVEN two restores at different epochs, THEN the Graph's physical failure schedule and every persisted counter are identical; only epoch-keyed threat draws differ. (vii) GIVEN a grep of the shipped source and data, THEN `threat_epoch` has zero hits (lint; positive control: a fixture containing it fails). Cites: SL-1, SL-23, T-6, T-8.",
 "145. **AC-SL-145 (auto, integration) — the four required restore-epoch cases and their failure paths** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R1 as amended by R13/R14)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated rulings R13, R14)*. (i) GIVEN one autosave restored by the death stub twice in one process, THEN the epochs are `e + 1` and `e + 2` and the kernel-derived threat draws (a spy on the kernel's `counter_eff` derivation, same `rng_counter`) differ. (ii) GIVEN a Save & Quit and a Continue of that newest `QUIT` generation in a fresh process, THEN the epoch is unchanged (`e`), no epoch write is issued, and the draws equal the uninterrupted run's (AC-SL-142); GIVEN the same `QUIT` generation not the newest (an `AUTO` written after it) or demoted, THEN the Continue of the selected generation advances it. (iii) GIVEN a process kill after an `AUTO` or `EVENT` generation and a fresh-process Continue, with `campaign.json` deleted before the relaunch, THEN the epoch advances to `e_slot + 1`, read from `slot_epoch.bin`; GIVEN `slot_epoch.bin` deleted or with a bad CRC32, THEN it reads as `max(newest verified generation's header copy, 0) + 1`, `SL_EPOCH_FILE_REBUILT` is logged, and that Continue advances it once more (copy + 2). (iv) GIVEN the same (save bytes, `restore_epoch`) pair run twice to `T + 3 600`, THEN `state_hash` and every draw are identical. (v) *Failure path.* GIVEN the `slot_epoch.bin` write failing (injected), and separately held past `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` (injected monotonic source), THEN `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` is logged, `save_status` reads `FAILED`, `request_restore` is still made with the advanced value, play reaches `RUNNING`, no frame in the interval blocked the main thread for longer than one poll, and the next write job rewrites `slot_epoch.bin`. (vi) GIVEN a kill at each step of the `slot_epoch` write (the T-6 fault-injection harness), THEN recovery finds `slot_epoch.bin` with the old or the new value and a valid CRC32, never neither, deletes the `.tmp`, and no restore was requested with an undurable value on the success path. (vii) GIVEN `restore_epoch = 2^32 − 1`, THEN the next advance saturates and logs, and no value ≥ 2^32 is written. (viii) GIVEN any number of restores of one generation, THEN its file bytes, trailer SHA-256 and `state_hash` read back unchanged (R14), so SL-12's REBASED baseline key is stable (AC-SL-138). (ix) GIVEN two restores at different epochs, THEN the Graph's physical failure schedule and every persisted counter are identical; only epoch-keyed threat draws differ. (x) GIVEN a grep of the shipped source and data, THEN `threat_epoch` has zero hits (lint; positive control: a fixture containing it fails). Cites: SL-1, SL-19, SL-23, T-6, T-8."),

47	## Player Fantasy
48	
49	*Indirect — the player never experiences a save system; they experience what it guarantees: **trust without a safety net**.*
50	
51	Persistence has no fantasy of its own. The promise comes from Pillar 5 — "losing the home-ship or a crewmate costs ship and body, never knowledge" — and from the user's binding rule for death: "This is like project zomboid, death is a bitch. It happens." The emotion this system must produce is that the player believes, without ever checking, that (1) the ship they welded is still there tomorrow exactly as they left it, (2) a death will cost them the minutes since the last autosave and nothing else, and (3) the game never records a moment it could have warned them about: it will not save while a crewmate is down, for ten seconds after one gets up, while a suit is in a critical state, while a warning the world owes them is still open, while a breach they cut is still uncapped, or (if Attention publishes it) during a breach phase (SL-5); and if a death follows a restore within ten seconds, the restore steps back past that save (SL-8) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. It does **not** promise to refuse every doomed moment: a death that arrives with no tell and gives the player more than ten seconds after the restore is the world's, not the save's (user ruling, OQ-40). They never feel *saved*; they feel *committed*. Death and quitting never buy back more than the minutes since the last autosave. *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
52	
53	> You never see the save. You see a ship you welded together last week, still breathing, still yours. You go one room deeper than is wise because if it kills you, it costs the minutes since the last autosave — not the hull, not the campaign. When you die, there is no screen: a breath of black, and you are standing where the world last stood still, in a world that has not forgiven or forgotten anything, including the room that killed you. The save never lies about the world and never rescues you from a mistake; it only refuses to record a moment it could have warned you about. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
54	
55	**The player never...** (each absence is a rule elsewhere in this document):
56	
57	| The player never... | Because | What they feel instead |
58	|---|---|---|
59	| sees a save happen as an event | capture stays inside the kernel's snapshot budget (`SNAPSHOT_BUDGET_MS`, cited from the kernel, not restated) and the write is off the critical path (SL-10) | the world runs continuously; the ship "just exists" |
60	| chooses which save to load after a death | the death stub restores the newest verified generation (SL-7, SL-8) | death is consequence, not a menu |
61	| sees a death screen, a thumbnail or a sting | SL-7, SL-21; art bible 7.4 "No death screen" | the loss lands in the body of the game, not in an interface |
62	| buys back a mistake at will | no save-anywhere in the MVP (SL-4) | weight on every door and every weld |
63	| wakes into a moment the game had already warned about *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | the autosave gate defers while any seat is `DOWNED` or `DEAD`, for `W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE` ticks after a recovery, while a seat is `CRITICAL`, while a Life-Support Graph warning window or a self-inflicted breach is still open, and (if Attention publishes it) outside a calm breach phase (SL-5); a death that follows a restore within `W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE` ticks steps back past it (SL-8); what the gate cannot see beyond that is not promised *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | a death that was warned about was theirs to avoid; one that came with no tell is the world's, not the save's |
64	| loses the campaign to one bad file | a rolling ring of `AUTOSAVE_GENERATIONS` 3 and a refuse-don't-corrupt pre-check (SL-3, SL-11) | the long tail is safe to invest in |
65	
66	**Honesty about the MVP (Pillar 5, second half).** "Never knowledge" is **mechanism-only** in the MVP: the PROFILE store exists and is tested with a synthetic block (SL-9), but no PROFILE block ships, and the kernel states that the MVP death stub "is a placeholder, not Pillar 5's failure contract". In the MVP the only knowledge that survives a death lives in the player's head — which, because the world is deterministic (SL-23), is genuinely reusable: the scrubber that failed at minute four fails at minute four again. That is a real, small, honest version of Pillar 5, and this section does not claim more. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The same determinism would also replay a *threat* draw (the ambush at the same corner) after a restore, which works against Pillars 2 and 3; by user ruling (D16, OQ-47) threat draws (Attention, Horror) re-key per restore epoch while the Graph's physical failures and every persisted counter replay exactly *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
67	
68	**The anchor moment (MVP, solo; numbers from SL-4, SL-5, SL-8 and the Controller's `DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS` 1800, at `TICK_RATE` 60).**
69	
70	1. **T = 432 000** (two hours of sim time). An interval autosave is written (kind `AUTO`). The player sees and hears nothing: there is no per-write mark of any kind (UI-1 retired). The pause panel shows no save fact at all, so a player who opens it learns nothing about when the game last wrote or deferred; the newest record's playtime (2:00:00) appears only on the main-menu Continue screen (UI-2, UI-4). *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
71	2. **T = 437 400.** The player completes their first weld; an event autosave is written (kind `EVENT`; 5 400 ticks since the last write, above `AUTOSAVE_MIN_GAP_TICKS` 1800). Again invisible.
72	3. The player pod-hops to a derelict and pushes one room too far. At **T = 446 400** their suit runs out of air mid-channel and `loco_state` becomes `DOWNED`. The next interval autosave falls due at T = 448 200 (437 400 + `AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_TICKS` 10 800); the gate refuses it: the save system will not record the trap (and had the suit been `CRITICAL` before the fall, the gate would already have deferred it softly, SL-5) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*.
73	4. **T = 448 200** (`DOWN_TO_DEATH_TICKS` 1800 = 30 s after the fall; a player who chose the solo `give_up` action would reach `DEAD` sooner, `GIVE_UP_MIN_TICKS` after the fall at the earliest, user ruling D7) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: `DEAD`. On that same tick's boundary the death stub requests a restore of the newest verified generation (the one from T = 437 400). No beat, no lights-out, no screen.
74	5. The kernel enters `LOADING`; the Pipeline shows layer-1 black (`TRANSIT_HOLD`). The black hold is bounded by `LOADING_TARGET_MS` (1000, provisional); under 120 ms reads as a flash, over about 2 s reads as a crash (Game Feel).
75	6. The first `RUNNING` frame is a hard camera cut to the avatar standing at the weld they just finished, at the **pre-load zoom** (the Pipeline keeps `k_z` across an in-session load), with one plain ship-log line from the HUD (placeholder: "Restored from the record at 2:01:30.", the restored generation's playtime, `437 400 div 60` = 7 290 s; UI-11) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. The new section is welded on. The pod is docked. The derelict still holds the room that killed them, and the physical world's keyed draws (the Graph's, set by step and subject) play out the same way if they walk the same path.
76	7. **The cost, in one sentence:** 10 800 ticks — three minutes of play — and nothing else. No item loss, no stat penalty, no progression tax.
77	
78	The anchor emotion is the half-second of black followed by recognition: *I am back at the weld. The ship is exactly as I made it. I know what is in that room now.* That is Zomboid's "death is a bitch" scaled to a three-minute window, with Pillar 5's kernel — the next attempt knows more — carried entirely by the player and the deterministic world. The typical loss is at most one `AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_TICKS`; **each death discards at most** 20 400 ticks (5.7 minutes), and 24 000 ticks after one step-back (6.7 minutes), **on a healthy writer and when the `DOWNED` episode that ended in death is the first since the last capture** (a crew revived and downed again adds up to 1 799 ticks per recovery, F-7) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* (Formulas, `loss_ticks`, `discard_per_restore`; the figures include the post-`DOWNED` refractory, user rulings) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. While writes keep failing the rewind grows with the failure (the backoff bounds the retry rate, not the loss), and the net progress lost across a step-back chain is larger than either number (`net_progress_lost`, F-7). Event saves lower the typical loss; the interval is the lever for the interval path. These numbers are the tuning surface of how much death hurts: playtest knobs, not designs of consequence. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
79	
80	**Design test (Pillar 5, applied).** *A save that lets the player buy back a mistake vs. a save that only refuses to record a moment the game could have warned the player about *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* → the refusal.* Concept test: "safe farming vs. scarcity that pushes inward → scarcity." Every dispute below resolves the same way:
81	
82	| Debate | Resolves to | Rule |
83	|---|---|---|
84	| Save-anywhere vs. autosave + Save & Quit | autosave + Save & Quit | SL-4 |
85	| Unconditional step-back after a second quick death vs. the newest verified generation | the newest verified; step back only when it fails verification, or when it is `RISKY` and the death came within `DEATH_LOOP_WINDOW_TICKS` of restoring it, or when the fall came within `W_MIN_WARNING_S × TICK_RATE` of restoring it, `RISKY` or not (the fairness step-back, user ruling X7) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* | SL-8 |
86	| Autosave while `DOWNED` vs. defer | defer | SL-5 |
87	| Let the player pick a generation after a death vs. the stub picks | the stub picks | SL-7, SL-8 |
88	
89	Secondary test (Pillar 1 applied to persistence): *a restore that re-presents the world as it was vs. one that re-presents what the player saw → as it was.*
90	
91	**Under hallucination (Pillar 4).** The save is the one artefact in the game that is pure ground truth. That deepens the horror if, and only if, the player can never use it as a free window onto truth. Pillar 4: "No lie is unfalsifiable: the truth is always available … and checking costs time, risk or trust." The rules (all enforced in SL-24 and its criteria):
92	
93	| # | Rule | Why it deepens rather than breaks the fantasy |
94	|---|---|---|
95	| H1 | A save stores SIM truth only: never a `PERCEPTION_OUT` block, never a "what the player saw" field, no thumbnail. | The record of the ship is incorruptible — the dead derelict's flight recorder, not a photograph of your madness. |
96	| H2 *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)* | Every persisted counter and seed (the owners' `rng_derive` counters, kernel G4 and D.10) is restored exactly, and Save/Load never varies by perception. Whether a **perception** draw (sanity drift, the onset of a false system state) replays identically after a restore or is re-keyed is **Sanity & Hallucination Rules' decision**, not this GDD's (OQ-37); any re-keying must not be steerable by the player, so quit and death offer no reroll oracle. Physical-world determinism (the scrubber that fails at minute four) is unchanged: that is Pillar 1. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: threat draws (Attention, Horror) are re-keyed per restore epoch by user ruling D16, OQ-47; they are not perception draws, and the Graph's physical failures and every persisted counter still replay exactly. The re-key keys off Save/Load's persisted `restore_epoch`, SL-23.)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R1: the epoch advances on every restore, death stub or load, and is durable before the first `RUNNING` tick; whether a Save & Quit followed by Continue should instead be exempt is a USER DECISION, OQ-50.)* | Binding perception replay into a Save/Load rule would turn hallucinations into fixed scripts the player can memorise across deaths, flattening dread (P2) and Discovery, which P4's "checking costs time, risk or trust" depends on. Save/Load states only what it owns: exact counters, no perception input, and no restore path that hands out a free reroll. |
97	| H3 | The sanity level is WORLD-scoped in the MVP and rolls back with the world. | Death is not a sanity cure: a player already low wakes still low; no "die to clear your head" exploit. |
98	| H4 | No clean frame: the first `RUNNING` frame after `LOADING` must already be presented through the Perception Filter for the restored sanity level; the black hold covers any rebuild. | One unfiltered frame would be a free oracle. This is a **routed request** to Perception Filter, Sanity and Pipeline (all three now designed; the ordering request stands, OQ-11), not Save/Load's to implement. |
99	| H5 *(Amended 2026-10-26 — CD-GDD-ALIGN)* | Every mark this system sources (the failed-write notice, the main-menu newest-record line, its strings) is an inviolable channel: it never carries flesh tones or violet, never flickers with sanity and is never faked by a hallucination class. There is **no per-write mark** in the MVP, so nothing on screen tells the player when the game saves or defers a save. | One more thing the player can trust absolutely. A per-write glyph was retired (UI-1): held by the gate, its absence would have signalled that danger was building, a hidden Attention meter against P3. |
100	| H6 | Save/Load never reads, derives or varies by perception: no sanity-dependent autosave timing, no hallucinated save list. | A lie that reached the save menu would be unfalsifiable inside the session; Pillar 4 requires at least one channel of truth to remain. |
101	
102	**Reference techniques — adopt / reject.**
103	
104	| Reference | Technique | Decision | Reason |
105	|---|---|---|---|
106	| Project Zomboid | Continuous autosave; Save & Quit only; no manual slots | **Adopt** | The user's stated touchstone (SL-4) |
107	| Project Zomboid | Permadeath of the character while the world persists; a new character | **Reject for the MVP** | The user rule is restart from the last autosave; the new-character form is Failure Contract & Re-wake's (VS-A) |
108	| Darkest Dungeon and roguelikes | No manual save; autosave on meaningful events | **Adopt** (event triggers, names provisional) | Weight on every decision |
109	| Roguelike "suspend save" (consumed on resume) | A quit-save deleted when resumed | **Reject** | A death after a Continue would lose more than the last autosave; contradicts SL-8 |
110	| Souls-likes | Authored bonfire-style rest points; a "YOU DIED" screen; a corpse run | **Reject** | Authored spatial rest points violate "no authored story"; a death screen is forbidden (art bible 7.4); a corpse run is a progression penalty |
111	| Most RPGs and immersive sims | Named manual save-anywhere; quicksave | **Reject** (MVP) | A reload becomes a free hallucination oracle and the cost of death vanishes; the one fallback is a pinned main-menu-only slot (OQ-18) |
112	| Rogue-lite meta progression | Unlocks earned by dying | **Reject** | Anti-pillar "nothing levels up"; would invert Pillar 5 (death becomes profitable) |
113	| Pandorum, *Beyond the Aquila Rift* | Waking into wrongness | **Route to Failure Contract & Re-wake** | The re-wake fiction is VS-A; using it in the stub would break SL-7 |
114	| Satisfactory and factory games | Saves as long-lived investment; patch-safe migrations | **Adopt the principle** | "Versioning is cheapest on day one"; golden saves (SL-14) |
115	| The save-thumbnail convention | A screenshot in the load list | **Reject** | It would capture the Perception Filter's lie (Pillar 1; SL-21) |
116	
117	**Anti-pillar guard rails.**
118	
119	| Anti-pillar / pillar | Guard rail for Save/Load |
120	|---|---|
121	| Not a game you win | No "final save", no completion flag, no ending state in the header; saves never close a campaign; `SaveInfo` carries no percentage and no progress meter |
122	| Not a freeform builder | No ship-blueprint export or import, no "save ship design"; the composite ship is Layout + Graph + Body data only |
123	| Not intentional PvP | Host-owned saves only; no guest-authoritative block; a friendly-fire death (VS-B) is Failure Contract's, never a save that records blame |
124	| Not an authored story | No named chapters, acts or authored save locations; generation labels come from SIM facts (the depth label is provisional from Web Map) |
125	| Not a combat game | The death stub attaches no penalty, no visible deaths counter and no difficulty tier; the cost is the autosave interval, nothing else |
126	| P2 Dread Before Chaos | The autosave gate is a Pillar 2 obligation, not a convenience: a save inside a `DOWNED` state, inside an open Graph warning window, or (if Attention publishes it) in a non-calm breach phase is deferred |
127	| P3 The Web Watches | No audio cue for saving (any sound is attributable by the web) unless Audio justifies one; Attention restores exactly; no meter is stored for display |
128	
129	**Tone and fixed terms.** The few strings this system sources are plain, factual and low-affect, in a ship-log register: never apologetic, never cute, no exclamation marks, no emoji, no colour from the sane/insane palette. Placeholder examples (final copy is UX's and the narrative director's): "Newest record unreadable. Continuing from the one before it." / "This save was made by an incompatible build." / "Restored from the record at 2:01:30." (the UI-11 line, user ruling D15) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*. Fixed terms: "restart from the last autosave", "death stub", "generation"; player-facing labels "Continue", "Save & Quit", "New campaign". Not used affirmatively anywhere in this document or in a string it sources: "reload last save", "respawn", "save point", "game over", "you died", "progress saved", "quicksave", and "slot" for the (invisible) ring.
130	
131	*(Framing: indirect — "what it lets you stop worrying about"; selected over the direct "the ship remembers you" framing, which would put infrastructure in the player's face, and over the diegetic cryo-bay framing, which belongs to Failure Contract & Re-wake; logged.)*
132	
133	## Detailed Design

SL-23 rewritten under R13/R14, keeping one set of names: (0) Storage. restore_epoch now lives in the per-slot file user://saves/<id>/slot_epoch.bin (u32 little-endian + CRC32). It is written as slot_epoch.tmp, flushed, renamed and re-read; a good re-read reports EPOCH_DURABLE. It is not in any generation file, so generation bytes, the trailer SHA-256 and every key derived from them never change. Each WORLD generation header keeps a read-only copy taken at write time. (1) When it advances (R13). A death-stub restore and FAULT_RECOVERY always advance it. A Continue of the newest non-demoted verified QUIT generation carries it unchanged and writes nothing. Any other Continue advances it. The advance is min(2^32-1, max(e_mem, e_slot)+1); a stub that finds nothing loadable does not advance it. (2) Durable before the restore is requested. The advance is written in a staging step before request_restore: the write is a job of its own on the worker, polled once per frame and never blocking the main thread. request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash) is called only after EPOCH_DURABLE. During the staging interval a restore_pending latch is held, the dead seat stays DEAD and the down sheet's last frame is held, for 1 frame normally and at most 30 frames (500 ms). (2a) Failure path, a listed exposure. On a write failure or timeout the restore still proceeds with the value in memory, SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE is logged, save_status = FAILED, and the write is retried with the next write job.
